archetype.name: Retooling (frontcourt-first)
archetype.definition: A team climbing out of three straight bottom-of-the-league seasons on the back of an elite big-man pairing, still short of a play-in-caliber roster around it.

report.headline: Davis has lifted Washington off the floor; a losing-team ceiling remains.
report.take:
Washington spent the last three seasons ranked 30th of 30 on this site, bottoming out at 17-65 last year with the league's worst defense. At 7-11 and 21st on the Teams tab, it is now a merely bad team rather than a historically bad one. The margin backs that up. Net Rtg is -5.1 (22nd), the record sits just one win above what the differential implies, and the 82-game pace is 32 wins. That is real progress and an honest picture: the record was not built on close-game luck.

The improvement is almost entirely on defense. Last year's 122.7 defensive rating is now 116.6, while the offense (111.5, 24th) is no better than last season's 111.0. The engine is the frontcourt, graded A-. Anthony Davis ranks 3rd of 86 on the power forward tab with a 3.3 BPM and an +8.5 On-Off, and Alex Sarr adds a 62.9 TS % as one of the league's better centers. Opponents still get into the paint constantly (Opp Rim Rate 32.6, 25th), but they finish poorly once there (63.2 %, 11th). The offense is an inside-out, Davis-and-free-throws operation. Washington ranks 8th in FT Rate and 27th in 3PA Rate, and it makes only 33.6 % of the threes it does take.

The numbers hide two things. First, the defense's best stat is its most fragile one. Opponents are shooting 33.0 % from three, 4th-best in the league, while the defense forces almost no turnovers (29th) and loses the defensive glass (DRB % 25th). The three-point luck is the part most likely to fade, and the rest of the defense doesn't take possessions away. Second, the guards and wings, graded D+ and D, are a drag. Trae Young's On-Off is -6.3 next to Kyshawn George's +8.7. Tre Johnson ranks 106th of 108 shooting guards with a 47.9 TS %. AJ Dybantsa is using 23.9 % of possessions at a 50.0 TS %.

The path has been jagged. Washington broke even in October with a slightly positive margin, then went 4-8 in November while allowing 118.25 a game. That stretch included an eight-game losing streak, the last 10 games are nine points a game worse than even, and only a three-game win streak against TOR, CHI and ORL steadied things. This is a low-30s-win team whose fate rests on Davis staying on the floor and on whether the perimeter group can stop giving back what the bigs build.

strengths.title: An elite frontcourt pairing
strengths.body: Davis is a top-three power forward on the site and the team's best player by every measure. He has a 60.4 TS % on a 29.2 USG % and the team is far better with him on the floor. Sarr adds efficient finishing and size, which is why the frontcourt grades A- while every other group sits in the D range. It lasts as long as Davis's availability does; he has played 16 of 18 games.

strengths.title: A defense no longer in freefall
strengths.body: The defensive rating has gone from the league's worst last season to 21st. Opponents' eFG % is 10th-best, and rim protection holds up even though opponents get there often. Part of that is real, since Davis and Sarr contest everything near the basket. Part of it rides on opponents' three-point shooting, which is the least stable piece.

strengths.title: Living at the free throw line
strengths.body: The offense can't shoot from three, but it gets to the line at the 8th-highest rate in the league. That fits a team that runs its offense through Davis in the post and on drives. It is a sustainable trait, and it keeps the offense from collapsing on cold shooting nights.

concerns.title: Defense leans on opponents missing threes
concerns.body: Opponents are shooting 33.0 % from three, 2.4 points under the league. Meanwhile Washington forces turnovers at the 29th rate and rebounds opponents' misses at the 25th rate. When that three-point luck normalizes, nothing else in the defense is taking possessions away to cover the difference. Expect the defensive rating to drift up.

concerns.title: Perimeter group gives it back
concerns.body: The backcourt grades D+ and the wings D. Opposing small forwards post the 28th-most combined points, rebounds and assists against Washington. Tre Johnson and Dybantsa are carrying real usage at poor efficiency. Young's -6.3 On-Off says the lineups around him have not worked. Unless the young wings grow into it, this caps the team's ceiling.

concerns.title: An offense without a shooting identity
concerns.body: The offense takes threes at the 27th rate, makes them at the 25th rate and is 27th on the offensive glass. That is why it sits 24th in offensive rating, essentially unchanged from last season. The defensive gains have not been matched on this end.

trend.note: Washington played an even October, then lost eight straight in November while allowing 118.25 a game before winning its last three. The last 10 games are well below its season margin, so the win streak is a bounce more than a turn.

weekAhead.headline: One stiff test, then two games it should win
weekAhead.body:
The week opens at home against Boston, the clear class of the three opponents. Boston ranks 3rd in Net Rtg, has a top-three defense and sits 6th on the site. Its record of 11-6 actually undersells it, with a W vs Pt Diff of -2. Boston keeps opponents away from the rim and out of the paint better than almost anyone, which is the worst possible matchup for a Davis-centric, free-throw-hunting offense. It also takes half its shots from three, a direct test of Washington's opponent three-point luck.

The back end is friendlier. Orlando returns to Washington just days after losing here by 20, and it sits 19th on the site with a -4.2 Net Rtg, so this is essentially a mirror-image team. Charlotte, on the road, is 28th with the league's worst offense and is the most turnover-prone team in the league. Washington's main risk there is the glass: Charlotte leads the league in rebounding percentage on both ends.

keyMatchups.title: Davis against Boston's rim wall
keyMatchups.body: Boston allows the 3rd-lowest Opp Rim Rate and holds rim shots to 61.0 %, while also allowing the fewest combined points, rebounds and assists against its own averages to opposing centers. Washington's interior offense is its entire offense. If Davis and Sarr get walled off, there is no three-point volume to fall back on.

keyMatchups.title: Orlando's soft spot at power forward
keyMatchups.body: Orlando gives opposing power forwards 25.31 points a game, 26th in the league, and allows opponents 38.7 % from three. That sets up well for Davis inside, and even Washington's poor shooters could find open looks. The 116-96 win on Nov 22 suggests the matchup is real.

keyMatchups.title: Charlotte's boards and giveaways
keyMatchups.body: Charlotte is 1st in ORB %, DRB % and REB %, against a Washington side 27th in REB %. Charlotte also turns it over more than any team, but Washington forces turnovers at the 29th rate and may not cash in. Winning this one comes down to Washington not letting Charlotte's offense live on second chances.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Boston's three-point barrage, at the league's 2nd-highest 3PA Rate, cracks Washington's 33.0 % opponent three-point mark, the first real test of how much of the defensive improvement is luck.

restOfSeason.body:
The 32-win pace is a fair starting point, and the margin supports it. There is no close-game cushion to give back, and the eight-game skid and three-game streak roughly cancel out. The defensive rating is the number most likely to move the wrong way as opponents' three-point shooting drifts back toward league average, since the defense creates so few extra possessions. The offense, built on Davis and the free throw line, should stay roughly where it is, which is bottom-ten. Expect something in the high-20s to low-30s in wins, a big jump on the last three years but below the play-in line in most scenarios.

The upside path runs through the perimeter. If Kyshawn George's strong On-Off holds and Dybantsa's efficiency climbs, the D-grade groups can stop bleeding points. The downside is simpler: this team is only respectable with Davis on the court, and any lengthy absence would drop it back toward the bottom tier.

confidence.note: 18 games; the margin and record agree, but the defensive three-point luck is a small, noisy sample.
